Keysight Technologies Inc reported results for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 with revenue of $1.85 billion, net income of $397 million and earnings per share of 2.82, 30.56% above the estimate [D1]. Revenue grew 36.54% on a year earlier and 7.51% on the quarter before, and net income grew 107.85% on a year earlier [D1]. The gross margin was 65.87% and the net margin was 21.51% [D1]. Total assets were $11.92 billion and stockholders' equity was $6.57 billion at the quarter end [D1]. Management described the quarter as one of record results with broad-based growth across its markets [D3].

The Communications Solutions Group reported revenue of $1.35 billion for the quarter, up 43.09% on a year earlier, and operating income of $458 million, up 86.18% [D1]. The Electronic Industrial Solutions Group reported revenue of $501 million, up 21.60% on a year earlier, and operating income of $155 million, up 68.48% [D1]. Operating income across the reported segments rose 81.36% on a year earlier [D1]. Management guides the fourth quarter to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 on 172 million diluted shares [D1]. The mid-point of the revenue range represents growth of 37% on a year earlier [D1]. Management raised its outlook for the fourth quarter and for the full fiscal year [D3].

Management said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue and that the supply environment is less flexible than a year earlier [D3]. Management said demand is not the limiter and that converting demand into revenue will remain nonlinear over the next several quarters [D3]. The company said it works with suppliers to deconstrain the supply chain and is taking a longer view of supply chain planning, including product redesigns to accommodate second-source components [D3]. Management said the one-time tariff impacts this year pulled up fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat [D3]. Management said integration of the acquired businesses is largely complete, one quarter ahead of schedule, with most of the planned cost synergies expected on a run-rate basis by the end of the fiscal year [D3]. Management said wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time [D3].

The market is weighing whether supply rather than demand sets the ceiling on revenue over the next several quarters [D3]. Analysts questioned whether demand is sustainable and whether supply constraints are limiting guidance [D3]. The bullish case rests on continued capital spending by hyperscale technology companies building AI infrastructure [D2]. Positive sentiment extended to other companies exposed to testing, measurement and photonics [D2]. The write-up warned that analyst price targets are treated with less skepticism than they deserve, because the firms setting them have business incentives that push the targets higher [D5]. The write-up said the shares carry its highest rank [D5]. Articles published alongside the call coverage question whether further stock price gains are supported by fundamentals [D3].
